title: [fields] formatDate's 'short' compact form keeps a Western field order after localization
body:
Observation-class, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a surprise. No user is blocked; nothing here is a regression.

## What it is

#4272 made `formatDate`'s `'short'` branch honor the threaded locale, but deliberately localized **only the month token** — the compact shape around it is assembled by hand:

```
const month = date.toLocaleDateString(options?.locale, { month: 'short' });
const day = date.getDate();
const year = String(date.getFullYear()).slice(-2);
return `${month} ${day}, '${year}`;
```

So a `zh` session renders `8月 15, '26`: a localized month inside a month-day-year layout with a Western comma and apostrophe-year. `zh`'s own compact convention would be year-first.

This was the ruled scope for #4272 and is correct as far as it goes — the alternative, handing the whole thing to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, changes the **English** output too (`Aug 15, '26` becomes `Aug 15, 26`, losing the apostrophe), which that card pinned as byte-identical must-not-change. So the mixed form is a deliberate consequence, not an oversight.

## Why it might still be worth a decision later

The compact form exists for narrow mobile cards, where the apostrophe-year is a density trick rather than a locale convention. Whether a `zh` / `ja` reader should get their own compact convention (`26/8/15`) instead of a localized token in a Western frame is a product call, and it trades against the byte-identical English pin. Recording it as an observation rather than proposing a change.

Only consumers today are ObjectGrid's two mobile-card date cells. Context: #4272, #4468 / PR #4512.
